races.name: Chloe Mediumship Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Trouville
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner with course-relevant Good-ground form and a Sean Bowen booking; the STYLE_FIT flag notes it races slightly out of role but here it is actually ideally suited — dictating from the front is precisely what this race shape asks of it, making the flag less damaging than usual.

runners_data.name: Biggles
runners_data.note: Tom Lacey's nine-year-old is the highest-rated runner on OR=120 but best form is over shorter and on Good; a natural hold-up horse whose deep finishing style is compromised by a one-pace leader setting a controlled tempo — the 50-day absence also adds minor uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Don De La Frontera
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and form figures of 78-7 offer little encouragement; one hurdles run at this trip on Good is the entirety of the hurdles evidence, and Jonathan Burke will need to engineer a prominent position from an unknown tactical base to have any impact.

runners_data.name: Bailey's Luck
runners_data.note: A genuine closer in style, fades-in-finish flag is a material concern over 2m on a well-run day; Clare Hobson's four-year-old has minimal hurdles experience and the hold-up approach at this trip behind a single tempo-setter looks structurally awkward.

runners_data.name: Likewhatyousee
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. on a horse that has won and placed prominently at 2m+ on similar ground; the in-form Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill yard (T14: 4/16) is the single most relevant trainer angle, and tracking Trouville closely is the natural shape for this runner.

runners_data.name: Tracker Issue
runners_data.note: Six starts without a win across soft and good ground, hold-up style, and a 35-day break — Ryan Mania will find the closers' highway congested with rivals in this hold-up-heavy field, and the 2m trip on Good has not brought the best out of this horse previously.

runners_data.name: Zerouali
runners_data.note: One run over hurdles — sixth over this exact trip on Good — provides a slender evidence base; Shane Quinlan takes a 3lb claim but the horse's hold-up profile means it is structurally waiting for a pace that may never materialise fast enough.

runners_data.name: Letmeseethecolts
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's five-year-old has a hurdles win and a recent second at 2m1f on Good, the strongest closer credentials in this field; Nathan Moscrop rides and while the hold-up style faces the usual structural challenge here, the form quality sets this apart from the other rear-runners.

runners_data.name: Miss The Sting
runners_data.note: Fades-in-finish flag on a horse that has never completed a hurdles win; the nine-day turnaround is short, the 2m trip on Good has produced a pulled-up and an eighth, and the hold-up style in a moderate-pace race points toward limited prospects.

runners_data.name: Whermyrosemarygoes
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden is a high-quality booking for Faye Bramley's unknown-style runner, and the 75-day layoff warrants monitoring; going is flagged UNKNOWN so Good-ground suitability is unproven, but if Cobden navigates a handy position this lightly raced mare could outrun odds.

runners_data.name: Amalfina
runners_data.note: Jack Hogan partners a mare with placed hurdles form at 2m on Good (third at Huntingdon); a natural hold-up type whose best results suggest she stays and handles the going, but the redistribution means she will not get a prominent pitch — this race shape asks her to produce a finish the tempo may not set up.

runners_data.name: Cool Million
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's four-year-old is lightly raced (two hurdles runs, third and fifth on Good ground at 2m); Harry Kimber rides and the unknown style means tactical flexibility is possible — a mid-division position could turn into an each-way platform if the pace is honest enough.

runners_data.name: Pearl Knot
runners_data.note: Oliver Greenall & Josh Guerriero's four-year-old has a hurdles unseating and a fifth to its name over this trip; Toby Wynne's assignment is tough with minimal data, unknown style, and a field of redistributed hold-up horses likely to crowd the same running lanes late.

races.paceDynamic: Trouville is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, will dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo from flag to finish on Good ground over Uttoxeter's 2m. Likewhatyousee is the only prominent racer capable of tracking close, meaning Trouville can set whatever fractions suit and arrive at the home straight with reserves intact. The hold-up battalion — Biggles, Bailey's Luck, Amalfina, Tracker Issue, Letmeseethecolts, Zerouali, and Miss The Sting — is substantial and will be forced to sit deep, making a late sustained challenge over this sharp 2m trip highly dependent on the pace being genuinely strong enough to string them out, which a lone front-runner rarely provides. This shape strongly favours the front-two positions: Trouville and any horse close enough to pounce from a stalking position, with hold-up horses at a structural disadvantage given the likely tempo control. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically get a clear run from deep; Biggles, Bailey's Luck, and Amalfina are redistributed to midfield on the map but are true closers who will not naturally secure prominent ground — Trouville and Likewhatyousee are most likely to occupy the front positions that matter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trouville Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Trouville bowls along at a measured, uncontested gallop and quickens from the front turning for home.
scenarios.body: Trouville dictates every fraction with Likewhatyousee the only horse close enough to pressurise, and on Good ground over 2m the lack of a genuine pace battle means the leader's energy reserves are never drained. Horses racing prominently or close to the pace are prime beneficiaries as the hold-up contingent simply cannot generate enough momentum from the rear to peg back a fresh front-runner.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalker Swoops Late Hurdle
scenarios.trigger: If Trouville sets just enough gallop that a well-positioned tracker delivers a clean jump at the last and gets up.
scenarios.body: Likewhatyousee, tracking smoothly throughout, produces the most likely version of this, arriving at the final flight with momentum behind a weakening Trouville. This scenario still requires proximity to the pace — it rewards the horse that travels best in the first two, not one coming from the back of the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Aids Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Trouville sets a surprisingly sharp gallop early, overcooks it, and fades badly before the last, opening the race for hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: Letmeseethecolts and Amalfina, who have shown placed form at similar trips on Good ground, would be best placed to capitalise from midfield if the tempo unexpectedly rises and the front-runners tie up. However, this scenario is discounted because a single uncontested front-runner rarely burns itself out, and many closers here carry redistribution penalties meaning they may not get a clear run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Hurdle Incident
scenarios.trigger: If a jumping error, interference, or fallers reshuffle the field mid-race, disrupting Trouville's rhythm and creating an open dash from the front.
scenarios.body: Unknown-style runners like Whermyrosemarygoes and Don De La Frontera, who carry tactical flexibility with light race records, could capitalise in a scrambled finish if the race loses its shape. This is a low-probability disruption scenario only worth noting because the novice field contains several lightly raced and unproven jumpers.

watchPoints.text: Likewhatyousee and Trouville — if Jonjo O'Neill Jr. slots directly behind Bowen from the outset, this race effectively becomes a two-horse duel from an early stage, and any gap opening between them and the field over the first mile is decisive.

Letmeseethecolts — the one hold-up horse with credible form quality; if Nathan Moscrop gets a wide-open passage turning in rather than meeting traffic, the closer threat becomes real and should not be dismissed simply because of race shape.

Whermyrosemarygoes — Harry Cobden's lightly raced unknown-style runner is the biggest wildcard; 75 days off, unproven going, but a top pilot who will manufacture a position — watch how she jumps the first two hurdles for a read on her confidence.

The redistribution cluster (Biggles, Bailey's Luck, Amalfina) — all three are genuine hold-up horses bunched together in the rear; if they meet traffic or interference with each other at any of the downhill hurdles, multiple runners may be knocked out of contention simultaneously, magnifying Trouville's advantage.

Miss The Sting — only nine days since last run and a fades-in-finish flag; if Lee Edwards is forced to push earlier than ideal to avoid the hold-up traffic, this runner's tendency to stop late will be exposed before the final flight.

races.name: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle Race (Div I)

runners_data.name: Versatile
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with consistent form at 16f on Good, placing three times in five recent runs at this course configuration; Alex Chadwick's 3lb claim helps the weights but from the rear this pace shape is unlikely to suit — needs stronger fractions than Chicago Storm is set to provide.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win but rock-solid, with four straight finishes between 3rd and 4th showing genuine consistency. Has run over today's trip and going before, rated 104, and the yard is firing at 34% over the last fortnight — a leading danger if that placed form finally converts.

runners_data.name: Alshadhian
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong placing record (1W6P) on similar going and ideal profile for tracking a single front-runner; Jack Tudor is an excellent pilot in these tactical contests, headgear includes a tongue-tie, and 17 days between runs suggests freshness without staleness.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win but placing regularly, with two runner-up efforts and two thirds across his last five starts, only fourth last time out. Has run over today's trip and going before, rated 106 here, well above his official mark of 98, and open to more.

runners_data.name: Chicago Storm
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who shapes to control this race entirely unchallenged, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) notes this is somewhat out of his usual role; his recent form (5F03-P) is patchy, and he's beaten only once on Good — the lone lead suits him tactically but his finishing effort is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Rated 115 here, a big jump on his official mark of 98, and enough to top this field despite recent efforts including a pulled-up run and a fall. Has run over today's trip and going before, and he remains the one to beat, though that indifferent form is the catch.

runners_data.name: American Empire
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse with an excellent placing record (1W5P) at 16f on Good and five consecutive runs at this course-distance profile; Donald McCain's yard has sent two runners in the last fortnight from a small yard, suggesting quiet confidence, and he should get a clear late run if the pace develops properly.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win but relentlessly consistent, third in each of his last three starts with a fourth and a second earlier in the sequence. Has run over today trip and going before, and our figure of 107 sits ten pounds above his official mark of 97, marking him a big threat.

runners_data.name: Iolaos du Mou
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse (headgear: hood) who has an outstanding Good-ground record at this distance (13/15 qualifying runs, 2W5P) and won at 16f on Good last time at this course; Tabitha Worsley is a competent claimer and the strong form line here is the most compelling of any hold-up horse in the race.
runners_data.comment: Won once in his last five and was runner-up earlier still, but consecutive sixths in his two latest starts show the form has cooled. Has run over today trip and going before, and our 97 sits just above his official mark of 93 for a fair profile.

runners_data.name: Auntie Maggie
runners_data.note: Prominent-style mare who has finished second twice over this course and distance on Good, making her a credible place contender tracking the pace; Ciaran Gethings is an experienced jump jockey and 37 days between runs leaves a small fitness query, but she profiles well for this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win, with a pulled-up run last time out the low point after a spell of midfield finishes including a 2nd. Has run over today's trip and going before, rated 96, a shade above her official mark of 91, and capable of better than that last effort.

runners_data.name: Colinski
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up type by history, this four-year-old is mapped to midfield because the rear of the field is oversubscribed; Charlie Maggs takes 3lbs off and recent form includes a third at this trip and going, but the STYLE_FIT discount (0.91) means he's unlikely to find his true position and may race with more pace than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win, with a 3rd and a 4th either side of an unseated in the past four starts, and a 5th his most recent effort nine days ago. Has run over today's trip and going before, rated 95, just above his official mark of 93.

runners_data.name: Ashdown Forest
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton reunites with this four-year-old after a 67-day break, which is the most significant concern here; his form figures (6776-) are uninspiring, his best going record comes from only 2 qualifying runs on similar ground, and although he's a true hold-up type he's been squeezed toward midfield by the crowded rear.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win, with the form consistently modest and nothing better than 6th across his last four starts. Has run over today's distance before, rated 94, and the yard's 29% strike rate over the last fortnight is about the best thing in his favour.

runners_data.name: Captain Connor
runners_data.note: The Good-ground record is very limited (1 qualifying run, 0W0P) and recent form in soft conditions has been modest at best; a four-year-old being forced off his natural rear-running style into midfield by the hold-up traffic jam, his chance hinges on conditions being faster than his form suggests suits him.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win and hard to fancy, with a 7th and a pulled-up run his last two starts, though a 4th and 3rd further back show he's not without ability. Has run over today's trip and going before, rated only 92, second from bottom in this field.

runners_data.name: Harry Gulliver
runners_data.note: Returning from 603 days off the track, which is the dominant factor in any assessment — no race fitness data to work from despite a solid historical record including wins at 20f on Good; Alex Hales sends him out from a quiet yard and the very long layoff must be treated as a serious risk until proven otherwise.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back, preceded by an unseated and an unplaced effort, though his last run was itself 603 days ago. Has run over today's trip and going before, rated 94, well above his official mark of 81, but that long layoff is the major query.

runners_data.name: Littletown Lad
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is damning in a race where hold-up runners need a strong late kick; recent form (06-87U) is poor, Sam England's yard has been active but this horse has shown nothing to recommend him in this field, and being pushed into midfield against his natural style compounds the problem.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win and rated bottom of this field on 89, with an unseated last time out capping a run that has yielded nothing better than 6th. Has run over today's trip and going before, but on this recent evidence he has a lot to find against these.

races.paceDynamic: Chicago Storm is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rivals able to get alongside in this congested field, is set to control from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m. Alshadhian and Auntie Maggie are the likeliest prominent settlers behind him, tracking close throughout, while the bulk of the 11-runner field — Versatile, American Empire, Iolaos du Mou and several true hold-up types — will fill midfield and rear. The field holds more genuine hold-up horses than can realistically find space at the back: Colinski, Ashdown Forest, Captain Connor, Harry Gulliver and Littletown Lad are all natural rear-runners but several will be forced to race closer than ideal, diluting the hold-up group's collective effectiveness. A single front-runner setting a measured pace on Good ground over a sharper 2m Uttoxeter circuit strongly favours horses racing prominently in second or third — close enough to pounce without burning energy in early congestion — and Alshadhian and Auntie Maggie are best placed to exploit that shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Chicago Storm sets a controlled, uncontested pace and prominent trackers travel smoothly throughout before asserting from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Chicago Storm's solo lead creates a soft early tempo that rewards horses travelling just behind the pace, with Alshadhian and Auntie Maggie ideally positioned to challenge approaching the last without having had to expend energy in a scrimmage. Good ground and a 2m trip at Uttoxeter suits this profile — horses prominent throughout who get first run on the closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Chicago Storm dictates entirely unchallenged and the pace is so modest that nothing can get to him from off it.
scenarios.body: With the tempo fully under his control and no rival willing to apply pressure, Chicago Storm could simply stay on from the front as the closers fail to close the gap from too far back in a slowly-run heat. This is a genuine outcome at Uttoxeter over 2m with a lone front-runner — the track is not so sharp that a strong front-runner is always caught.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Horses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and the true hold-up runners find a clear run to deliver a late challenge.
scenarios.body: American Empire and Iolaos du Mou are the most credible hold-up horses who may find room late if the race is run at a searching enough gallop; Iolaos du Mou has strong form at 16f on Good and would benefit from a strong pace draining the prominent horses. However, this depends on a pace that Chicago Storm's solo lead makes unlikely, capping the probability of this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Congestion Chaos Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a mid-race incident, fall or bunching disrupts the field and produces a messy finish where runners are shuffled out of position.
scenarios.body: With 11 runners over hurdles on Good ground and a compressed midfield group of hold-up types forced closer than natural, the risk of interference or a mistake affecting one of the prominent pair is real; the beneficiary would most likely be whichever hold-up horse avoids trouble and gets a clean run. Colinski or Harry Gulliver, arriving late from unpredictable positions, could emerge as unlikely winners.

watchPoints.text: Chicago Storm — if he jumps cleanly and establishes an uncontested lead, the entire race shape pivots on whether he is ever pressured; watch whether Alshadhian or Auntie Maggie close up enough early to apply psychological pressure or allow him to coast.

Iolaos du Mou — the outstanding Good-ground form record (13/15) and two course-distance wins make him the most dangerous hold-up runner if the pace quickens mid-race; watch for Tabitha Worsley angling for a gap approaching the final two hurdles.
Harry Gulliver — 603 days off the track is a serious unknown for any handicapper; watch closely in the pre-parade ring for signs of condition and temperament before forming any view.

Colinski and Ashdown Forest — both genuine hold-up types forced into unfamiliar midfield positions by the compressed rear group; watch whether they settle or run too freely, as either outcome could compromise their finishing kick late on.

Littletown Lad — flagged for fading and showing poor recent form; watch early to see if Jonathan England attempts to switch riding tactics, though any deviation from hold-up style in this field is likely to create further problems rather than solve them.

races.name: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle Race (Div II)

runners_data.name: Four Decades
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse dropping in slightly from longer trips, with no wins or placed efforts from six Good-ground runs at this trip — weak sim-going profile and 109 days off the track make this a speculative reappearance.|
runners_data.comment: Four Decades has been below her best of late, without a win in five starts and a best finish of fourth. She has run over today's trip and going, and a rating of 101 keeps her involved, though a 109-day absence is a concern.

runners_data.name: Belcamo
runners_data.note: Won on Soft last time and has placed four times from 15 Good-ground starts, returning after just 23 days for Alex Hales; a genuine hold-up type who needs the pace to be honest to be delivered from behind.|
runners_data.comment: Belcamo won two starts back, and was runner-up five starts back, with a below-par sixth last time out the blemish. He has run over today's trip and going, fit off a 23-day break, and a rating of 106 makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Jet Patrol
runners_data.note: Two wins and three places from nine Good-ground runs, with a recent fourth over this C&D trip on Good — Sean Bowen in the saddle for a shrewd yard, and this horse has a genuine record of delivering off a hold-up ride at Uttoxeter.|
runners_data.comment: Jet Patrol's only win in his last five starts came four starts back, sandwiched between modest efforts, and he was pulled up three starts ago. Fresh off a 23-day break and from an in-form yard, but a rating of 93 leaves him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Thickthorn Tom
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: unbeaten in three starts when making the running or going prominent, wears a tongue-tie, quick turnaround of just 8 days but the Skelton team fire horses fit — the step back to 2m from 2m5f-2m7f trips is the key query.|
runners_data.comment: Thickthorn Tom is in tremendous heart, with three wins from his last five starts including two of his last three, the other two runner-up finishes. Fresh off just eight days and race-fit, a rating of 99 is well justified by that rich sequence.

runners_data.name: Mayday Games
runners_data.note: Won last time out on Good but carries a "fades in finish" flag and a low trainer strike rate; though shown in midfield on the map, this horse's true profile is a hold-up type and the redistribution means it is unlikely to get a clean run from its natural position.|
runners_data.comment: Mayday Games won last time out, having overcome a fall three starts back and a pulled-up run before that, with only an unplaced effort between. A rating of 94 keeps him well in this mix on the back of that improving sequence.

runners_data.name: Cawthorne Banker
runners_data.note: Two wins and five places from 11 Good-ground starts — strong course form and wears a hood; Jonjo O'Neill Jr takes over and the horse won last time; genuine hold-up profile shuffled into the midfield band by the crowded rear.|
runners_data.comment: Cawthorne Banker won last time out, following a runner-up effort two starts back and continuing an upward trend after modest form earlier. A rating of 95 makes him competitive here on that improving profile.

runners_data.name: Ocean Heights
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with two wins from 15 Good-ground runs, best form came over slightly further trips; wears a tongue-piece, has a 5lb claiming rider, and its hold-up style is squeezed by a field stacked with closers.|
runners_data.comment: Ocean Heights is admirably consistent, third in three of his last four starts, but remains without a win. A rating of 99 is well clear of his official mark, leaving him just needing to get his nose in front.

runners_data.name: Castle Quarter
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old wearing a visor, one win from eight Good-ground runs at this trip; form string shows a 5th and a 7th in recent starts, and though its true style is hold-up, it is mapped to midfield simply because the back of the field is over-crowded.|
runners_data.comment: Castle Quarter is winless in his last five starts, with a pulled-up effort four starts back the low point, though a third-placed run five starts back shows some ability. A rating of 94 is well clear of his official mark.

runners_data.name: Genbu
runners_data.note: Consistent four-year-old with seven placings from 10 Good-ground starts and a win on this trip; prominent style suits this race shape well and Charlie Price has ridden it to place consistently — the youngest horse in the field but lightly built and travels with zest.|
runners_data.comment: Genbu won four starts back and followed up with back-to-back thirds, before a fifth last time out ended that sequence. A rating of 93 leaves him some way behind the pace-setters here.

runners_data.name: Fond Farewell
runners_data.note: Has an 'F' and a 'U' in the recent form, raising jumping reliability concerns; a natural hold-up type re-slotted into midfield by the map because the field is saturated with closers, and the poor jumping record is a real risk at any price.|
runners_data.comment: Fond Farewell is winless in his last five starts, with a fall, a pulled-up run and an unseated rider among them, and only a fourth to show on the plus side. A rating of 75 leaves him bottom of this field.

races.paceDynamic: Thickthorn Tom is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner handicap hurdle and, with no genuine rival to press him, Harry Skelton can dictate a comfortable, controlled gallop from the outset on Good ground at Uttoxeter. Genbu is the only other prominent-style runner and will look to track closely in second, meaning the early tempo is unlikely to be extreme — this shapes as a moderate-pace, leader-controlled contest where the front two set the terms unchallenged. The large hold-up contingent — Four Decades, Belcamo, Jet Patrol, Mayday Games, Cawthorne Banker, Ocean Heights, Castle Quarter and Fond Farewell — will be forced wide of their natural positions given the sheer volume of closers in the field, and several (Mayday Games, Cawthorne Banker, Ocean Heights, Castle Quarter, Fond Farewell) are redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the rear is over-subscribed; Thickthorn Tom and Genbu are most likely to actually secure the front two berths. This race shape — a single unhurried front-runner on Good ground over 2m — strongly favours horses that can travel prominently or make a forward move from midfield from the second-last, rather than deep closers who need a searching gallop to be delivered.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Thickthorn Tom dictates an uncontested moderate gallop and the pace never truly quickens until after the last, rewarding those on or near the pace.
scenarios.body: Thickthorn Tom controls every yard, with Genbu the only shadow; the pack is strung out chasing a false rhythm and the closers simply have too much ground to make up from the home turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Beats Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the front pair set enough of a tempo that their stamina is tested from three out, opening a late lane for the best travellers from midfield.
scenarios.body: Horses like Jet Patrol and Cawthorne Banker, who have course and distance winning form on Good ground, pick off a tiring Thickthorn Tom between the last two flights.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Weakens Late
scenarios.trigger: If Thickthorn Tom, who steps back in trip after runs at 20f-21f, finds 2m on Good ground too sharp in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: The leader capitulates after the last, and Genbu — already travelling prominently — is best placed to inherit, with Jet Patrol also finishing strongly from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If an unusually brisk early pace burns off the front pair and the redistributed hold-up horses manage to find their natural deep-closer role.
scenarios.body: Belcamo, who has four placings from 15 Good-ground starts and ran a creditable second last time, or Four Decades come from off the pace to catch a strung-out field — though this shape is the least likely given the field structure.

watchPoints.text: Thickthorn Tom's last four runs were all at 19f-21f — watch whether Harry Skelton allows him to bowl along freely at 2m or whether the drop in trip leaves him flat-footed from the second-last; his ability to see out the trip is the single biggest race-shaping factor.

Genbu is the only horse likely to sit directly on Thickthorn Tom's quarters — if Charlie Price decides to challenge from the home turn rather than wait, this could force the pace into something far more searching than the map suggests.

Fond Farewell has a 'F' (fell) and a 'U' (unseated) in its last six starts — with a field of 10 jumping 2m of hurdles on a tight track, any jumping incident from this horse could compromise multiple rivals at a crucial stage.

Cawthorne Banker won last time and Jonjo O'Neill Jr is a high-value booking — watch for an aggressive move from the second-last if the hold-up horses can find daylight, as the Good ground suits this horse's profile markedly better than Soft.

The volume of redistributed hold-up horses (five runners) means the home-turn bunching risk is elevated — watch for crowding between the last two flights if the pace is moderate and the entire field arrives upsides simultaneously.|

races.name: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Normofthenorth
runners_data.note: Course specialist with three recent runs at Uttoxeter including a win and a second both on Good going over 2m4f-3m; drops back to a front-running role he can dominate here, but the amateur claimer, 168lbs, and age 12 temper confidence that he can sustain the effort to the line.
runners_data.comment: Normofthenorth was fourth last time out, but won two starts back, and was runner-up three starts back, so the overall form is solid. A rating of 111 puts him right behind the selection, with that below-par run last time the only knock.

runners_data.name: Jongleur d'Etoiles
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden's booking for Neil Mulholland is a strong positive — trainer firing 2/10 in 14 days — and this 7yo has a second at 26f on Good in his recent history; prominent style suits the anticipated race shape ideally, and he is one of the most natural inheritors of position if the leader softens.
runners_data.comment: Jongleur d'Etoiles is winless in his last five starts, with a fall and a pulled-up run among them, though runner-up both two and five starts back. A rating of 95 leaves him a bit to find off a 48-day break.

runners_data.name: Betty's Tiara
runners_data.note: Has filled the frame consistently in similar fields including a third at 22f Good and multiple top-4 finishes, but the form string shows a downward curve recently (3-4-6-7-9) and Ben Pauling's yard is 0/4 in 14 days; prominent style is right but her rating trajectory is a concern at OR 100.
runners_data.comment: Betty's Tiara arrives on the back of a moderate sequence, sliding from third five starts back to ninth last time out. A rating of 104 marks her out as capable of far better, with that recent decline the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Jullou De Grissay

runners_data.name: Kenzo Des Bruyeres

runners_data.name: Slaney Opera

runners_data.name: Collingham

runners_data.name: Queens Wish

runners_data.name: Izzy's Grey

races.paceDynamic: Normofthenorth is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner handicap chase over 3m at Uttoxeter, and with no genuine rival looking to press for the lead, he is likely to control proceedings from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground. The prominent trio of Jongleur d'Etoiles, Betty's Tiara, and Slaney Opera will track him in the first rank, creating a compact, organised lead group rather than a pressured, strung-out tempo. The hold-up contingent is substantial — Kenzo Des Bruyeres, Queens Wish, Jullou De Grissay, and Collingham are genuine hold-up types, but the map is also carrying Jack's A Legend, Izzy's Grey, Uncle Al, Jo Arengeot Bey AA, Of Corse I Can, and Miami Jim in midfield when their true nature is hold-up; those horses are unlikely to find genuine cover at the rear in a field this competitive, and the most natural front-position claimants — Normofthenorth leading, with Jongleur d'Etoiles and Slaney Opera tracking — are best placed to secure their roles. A single-paced, honest gallop set by one controlled leader on Good ground over 3m classically favours prominent racers with stamina and jumping fluency who can pounce from close range at the second-last, rather than genuine closers who need a fast pace to generate ground from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Normofthenorth Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Normofthenorth bowls along unchallenged and the pace remains honest but not furious, setting up a stamina-based finish from 2 out.
scenarios.body: The leader shapes the race perfectly for horses tracking in second or third who conserve energy through the middle stages and produce a sustained run from the final bend; over 3m on Good ground at Uttoxeter this is the bread-and-butter outcome when one horse dictates. Prominent runners with proven stamina and jumping accuracy are the primary beneficiaries, able to collar the front-runner or hold on as closers fail to generate enough momentum from too far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Land Decisive Late Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is genuinely strong enough that the lead group tire in the final circuit, allowing the better-handicapped hold-up horses to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Kenzo Des Bruyeres and Queens Wish are the hold-up runners with the clearest profile to benefit, having shown finishing ability at this trip on Good ground, but the scenario requires the pace to be faster than one lone front-runner typically generates. This is attainable but requires Jongleur d'Etoiles or Slaney Opera to press Normofthenorth earlier than ideal, lifting the tempo sufficiently to crack the front rank.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Gallops Rivals Into Submission
scenarios.trigger: If Normofthenorth finds his best form and the prominent trackers are unable to sustain their challenge from three out, leaving him to score wire-to-wire.
scenarios.body: At OR 100 and aged 12, Normofthenorth has the course form and the tactical advantage of uncontested control, and his recent second at the same distance on Good ground shows he retains ability; a moderate pace that he dictates entirely can turn this into a test of jumping accuracy over stamina. His 168lb burden and amateur rider are the caveats, but if the race is run at his tempo he is the form pick for a front-running scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Chaos Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or a bunched finish with heavy traffic causes disruption in the closing stages, elevating lower-ranked runners.
scenarios.body: With 14 runners over fences on Good ground, jumping errors at key fences can dramatically reshuffle the field; Jo Arengeot Bey AA and Uncle Al, both recent winners at this trip, could emerge from the chaos if the market leaders are hampered or fall. This scenario is low probability but non-trivial given the size of the field and the presence of several horses with recent pulling-up or falling entries in their form strings.

watchPoints.text: Slaney Opera ran only 4 days ago and returns with course form at 26f Good — watch whether the short turnaround leaves her fresh or jaded, as she is ideally placed in the race shape but fitness management is the critical variable.

Kenzo Des Bruyeres with Sean Bowen — Mickey Bowen's yard has produced 3 winners in 15 days and this booking from a powerful jump jockey for a family yard is the most significant market mover to track before the off.

With 14 runners over fences, the field is large enough that a jumping incident at an early fence could compress the order and directly compromise the front-runners who set the early pace — watch Normofthenorth's jumping in particular at the first open ditch.

Miami Jim is 217 days absent and pulled up last time — if sent off at a surprisingly short price, treat with extreme scepticism; a horse returning from that layoff in hold-up style in a field this size is a notable risk to orderly finishes if he tires and sprawls at a late fence.

Jo Arengeot Bey AA won last time out at 24f Good for Donald McCain (trainer 2/12 in 14 days) — monitor market moves as the yard has had recent winners and the horse arrives in form, despite its hold-up profile being less suited to the anticipated pace shape.

runners_data.name: Dr Seb

races.paceDynamic: Kom Tu Voudras is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine rival to press it from the outset — it can dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over 2m7½f on good ground at Uttoxeter, a track that rewards horses ridden prominently throughout. Behind it, the race is cluttered with prominent-types — Mistral Blue, Lady Caro, Catuaba, Belladinotte, and others — who cannot all secure their natural position and will be forced to race in a more restrained midfield role than they prefer, creating a bunched, tactical chase pack rather than a true pressure-group. The hold-up horses (Billy Boi Blue, Seeitoldya, Baltray, Rock Hurley, Victoria Milano) will be further back still, needing a strong enough gallop to close off — and with only one horse genuinely setting the pace, that injection may come too late over this marathon trip. This race shape heavily favours runners who can track Kom Tu Voudras from second or third early and travel smoothly — the premium position is directly on the leader's heels — and redistributed prominent types who find themselves trapped in midfield will find it difficult to deliver a winning challenge from out of their comfort zone.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kom Tu Voudras Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Kom Tu Voudras bowls along at its own tempo unchallenged and the midfield pack never coalesces into a genuine threat.
scenarios.body: Kom Tu Voudras, trained by Faye Bramley and ridden by Harry Cobden, dictates throughout on its favoured good ground and simply stretches clear from the last flight as rivals struggle to close from a congested midfield; horses who track it closely early — Colegram and Orange Diamond — are best placed to capitalise if it tires.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If a close-tracking prominent type — Colegram, Orange Diamond or Prince De Juilley — sits second or third throughout and overpowers Kom Tu Voudras from the second-last.
scenarios.body: The moderate pace set by a single front-runner over 2m7½f enables a fresh, well-handicapped stalker to travel comfortably throughout and produce a strong finishing effort without burning energy early; Colegram's excellent recent form (311-31) and Dan Skelton's powerful in-form stable make it the standout beneficiary, with Orange Diamond's three wins on good ground also relevant.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Through
scenarios.trigger: If Kom Tu Voudras sets a genuinely strong tempo for this trip and the prominent pack chases it hard enough to open a late lane for closers.
scenarios.body: Billy Boi Blue or Baltray, racing from their natural hold-up berth, would need an uncharacteristically hot pace to reel in leaders — Rock Hurley, a recent course-relevant winner, represents the most interesting closer given Donald McCain's current form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent-types causes early positional scrimmaging that disrupts Kom Tu Voudras's rhythm and produces a muddling, stop-start gallop.
scenarios.body: Horses like Mistral Blue or Lady Caro, forced out of their natural roles, occasionally find improved position by accident when the field shuffles mid-race; at longer prices, Mistral Blue's three wins on good ground and Fergal O'Brien's eye for placing a handicapper give it some each-way appeal in a chaotic shape.

watchPoints.text: Kom Tu Voudras is the only genuine front-runner in a 16-runner field and Harry Cobden will control the race from flag to finish — watch whether it can sustain a long-run gallop or gets caught late.

Catuaba returns from 654 days off and blinkers may be applied for the first time — monitor the horse closely in the parade ring and early in the race for any signs of over-exuberance or jumping errors after such a prolonged absence.

The cluster of Mistral Blue, Lady Caro, Belladinotte, and Catuaba all want prominent position and all will be frustrated — watch for a scrimmage in the first half-mile as these horses contest for ground that simply does not exist, which could cause interference or knock several runners out of contention early.

Rock Hurley (William Maggs, 3lb claim) is the most interesting hold-up horse based on very recent good-ground winning form at 23f — watch how quickly it travels once the field settles, as its chance depends entirely on whether the Kom Tu Voudras-led tempo is truly genuine.

Colegram's Harry Skelton is likely to position the horse in second or third from the outset — watch whether Dan Skelton's stable runner can slot in directly behind Kom Tu Voudras, as that tactical position is arguably the most valuable in this race shape.

The yard is firing at 29% over the last fortnight, and with today's distance and going covered before, he rates 107, down among the outsiders on our figures.

runners_data.name: Jammy Jay
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 99, this natural front-runner is likely to find himself further back than he wants given the competitive prominent traffic; no wins from 11 runs on Good or Good-to-Soft is a stark record, and Ben Poste will need things to fall perfectly.|
runners_data.comment: A runner-up last time out is the highlight of an otherwise modest recent record that includes a well-beaten eighth. Rated five pounds above her official mark, she has raced over today's distance and going before but sits bottom of this field on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Dream Diamond is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in an 11-runner field, is expected to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable gallop over 2m4f on Good ground at Uttoxeter. The field carries a significant volume of prominent-racing types — Crystal Glance, Magical Hill, Wudya, and Jammy Jay are all natural front-end horses who cannot all secure their preferred position and have been redistributed to midfield on the pace map. Of those, Dream Diamond and Divilabother are best placed to hold a true forward pitch, with Pike Road and Golden Maverick also likely to press early. The result is a race run at a controlled, honest tempo — not a dawdle, but not a true test of stamina — which strongly favours hold-up horses and genuine closers who can pick off a tiring front rank in the straight, or a well-rated prominent type with enough tactical speed to sit just off the pace and pounce.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Diamond sets a sustainable gallop and the prominent cluster cancels each other out, leaving fresh legs at the rear to deliver late.
scenarios.body: Dream Diamond dictates a steady rhythm that suits horses held up off the pace, as the prominent types who have been squeezed back burn energy jostling for position mid-race. Hold-up runners such as Maghlaak, Dream's Ka and Gardener arrive with a decisive late run in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely honest and a well-positioned prominent horse travels smoothly to lead at the second-last without being seriously pressured.
scenarios.body: Divilabother, who has won twice recently on Good ground at this trip, is ideally suited to sitting just off Dream Diamond's pace and taking over turning in, while Pike Road or Golden Maverick could also land a blow from close range. This scenario rewards horses with a combination of tactical position and jumps fluency.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Diamond is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets only a modest pace that morphs into a stamina-sapping grind in the final mile.
scenarios.body: A lone front-runner on Good ground who meets every hurdle well and is never asked a question until the home turn can steal a march on a field full of horses racing out of their natural position. Dream Diamond's Good-ground record (12 of 14 runs) is a genuine asset here if connections ride with confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded prominent brigade causes interference or a false pace, triggering a scramble for position that suits the boldest jumper to capitalise.
scenarios.body: With Crystal Glance, Wudya, Magical Hill and Jammy Jay all naturally wanting to race forward but forced to settle, any early jostling or jumping error could break the race open chaotically. In that scenario, a horse with clean jumping and a degree of versatility — Dream's Ka or Gardener — benefits from others' misfortune.

watchPoints.text: Dream Diamond is the only true pace-setter — if Jonathan Burke chooses to back off the gallop and sets a crawl, the entire pace map shifts and hold-up horses may be left with no race to run into.|

Crystal Glance, Magical Hill, Wudya and Jammy Jay are all naturally forward-going horses who cannot all race where they want — watch the first three furlongs for scrimmaging and potential early interference among this prominent cluster.|

Dream's Ka is stepping up from a maximum of 20 furlongs to 24 furlongs (2m4f) for the first time — if Harry Skelton has to commit earlier than ideal because the gallop is slow, the stamina question becomes live.|

Divilabother arrives on the back of two consecutive wins and is the most in-form runner in the race; watch whether Harry Reed rides positively to sit just off Dream Diamond, as that would make him the one to beat entering the final flight.|

Golden Maverick has not run for 422 days and the fitness angle is unresolved — watch in the paddock and early in the race for any signs that the layoff has blunted his sharpness, which would effectively remove a prominent contender from the equation.|

races.name: Eleven Eleven Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Duke Of Luckley
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner at OR 122 with a strong recent record on good ground (14/15 similar-going starts in-frame), yet his last three runs show placed efforts only — he sets the tempo here but his tendency to be caught late under a forcing role is worth noting; Freddie Keighley (5lb claim) takes a little pressure off the weight.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, having won two starts back, with three pulled-up efforts before that. Has run over today's trip and going, and rated the number one in this field, he still looks the one to beat despite a stop-start campaign.

runners_data.name: Schmilsson
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes over on this OR 120 seven-year-old who won on his reappearance 21 days ago over this identical 2m trip on good; a confirmed prominent racer who loves these conditions (7/15 similar-going) and has the form to challenge a front-runner in the closing stages.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, with back-to-back wins four and five starts back the highlight of a solid campaign. A 5th and 4th sit in between, but he has run over today's trip and going, and is rated second in this field on 124.

runners_data.name: Seeyouinmydreams
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse from the T Ellis yard who finished a solid fifth last time after back-to-back seconds; versatile going record (11/15 similar-going) and a win over 2m good ground gives him the right profile to come home late if the pace is strong enough.
runners_data.comment: A model of consistency, with a win three starts back flanked by a third and a runner-up finish and nothing worse than 5th. Fifth last time out having been off 38 days, but she has run over today's trip and going before and rates a threat on 122.

runners_data.name: Gaelic Rambler
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. partners this progressive six-year-old for a yard in flying form (4/16 T14); his best form is on softer ground and his hold-up style means he needs something to collapse in front — the 2m trip on good is on the sharp side for him.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts but rarely far away, with two runner-up finishes and nothing worse than 5th. Third last time out, has run over today's trip and going before, and rated 118 he's a threat if that placed form finally converts.

runners_data.name: Merely A Detail
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old who won at this trip on good last time out (1/16f/GOO), and Jonathan Burke can push forward early; the trainer's low recent strike rate (0/1 T14) is a mild negative but the horse's form trajectory is the right way.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, but the four starts before yielded nothing better than 3rd, leaving her rated only 110 in this field. She has run over today's trip and going before, so the latest success aside, there's little here to suggest she troubles the leaders.

runners_data.name: Ice Jet
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's four-year-old is mapped to midfield yet his natural instinct has been to track the pace or come from off it — three wins at 2m½f suggests 2m on good might be quick enough; Harry Skelton's booking is obviously significant and his chase form (3W from 5 recent runs) is outstanding.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in the last five starts underline strong recent form, with runner-up efforts last time out and five starts back the only blips. Has run over today's trip and going before, rated 116, with the yard among the in-form trainers at 29% over the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Dog Fox
runners_data.note: Prominent racer at OR 102 who has failed to win any of his last three completed starts; Jack Tudor has the profile to get him handy and jumping well, but his form figures — including a fall and pulled-up — over similar trips suggest he needs things to go right at the fences.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in this sequence, with two thirds either side of a fifth and a pulled-up run, and an unseated effort before that — a mixed picture. Has run over today's trip and going before, rated 112 here, well above his official mark of 102, hinting at more to come.

runners_data.name: Rocks Up Late
runners_data.note: A genuinely front-running type in nature whose last win came over 17f on good (1/17f/GOO), but in a field loaded with prominent horses he is unlikely to achieve the position he needs — his best chance hinges on the race falling apart rather than a clean tactical execution.
runners_data.comment: Rated bottom of this field on 103, with finishes of 7th either side of a win two starts back — an inconsistent record. Has run over today's trip and going before, and needs more than one good effort in five to trouble this field.

runners_data.name: Ghasham
runners_data.note: Sam England's seven-year-old is a true hold-up horse by inclination (three placed efforts from close to the rear), pushed into a midfield slot on the map only because the real rear-runners are crowded out; recent form (2213) is solid but 2m good at Uttoxeter is a touch sharp for his style.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner two starts back with back-to-back runner-up efforts before that, for solid form on paper. Rated only 105 here, second from bottom in this field, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Duke Of Luckley is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pressing rival likely to sit on his shoulder, he should be able to dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over this 2m chase trip at Uttoxeter on good ground. Schmilsson and Merely A Detail are the other natural prominent types who will push forward early, but neither has the profile to significantly pressure Duke Of Luckley for the lead, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly searching. This field contains more prominent/front-running types than the race shape can accommodate: Rocks Up Late is a genuine prominent racer who will be squeezed back from his natural position, and Ghasham — a natural hold-up horse — is similarly displaced in the map, meaning neither will operate from their optimal spot. A controlled, front-runner-dictated gallop on good ground at an honest but not punishing pace strongly favours prominent-to-mid-pack types with class and a turn of foot — horses that can travel comfortably just off the leader and produce a clean jump at the last to settle it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Duke Of Luckley Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Duke Of Luckley is allowed to bowl along at his own tempo unchallenged and the pace remains controlled throughout.
scenarios.body: Duke Of Luckley sets a measured gallop and the race is run to suit horses travelling comfortably in behind before a decisive move two out; the premium positions just off the pace become the winning zone.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Clash
scenarios.trigger: If Schmilsson or Merely A Detail refuses to settle and presses Duke Of Luckley into a stronger gallop than he intends.
scenarios.body: A more genuine pace develops, stretching the field and gradually exposing stamina reserves; horses who handle a stiffer test and can sustain their effort to the line benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final circuit and the lead group ties up, handing late momentum to those held off the pace.
scenarios.body: Ice Jet, despite his redistribution note, has genuine finishing gears and could pick up a weakening field; Seeyouinmydreams also has the profile to swoop if the gap appears late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Errors
scenarios.trigger: If jumping mistakes or early incidents disrupt the anticipated race shape and reshuffle positions significantly.
scenarios.body: Carnage at fences can wipe out the expected leaders and hand the initiative to horses capable of improvising tactically; Dog Fox at a big price and Gaelic Rambler, both proven over fences, could capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Duke Of Luckley and Schmilsson will be racing in close proximity early — watch for either horse getting outpaced or crowded at the first fence, which could instantly alter the anticipated controlled gallop.

Rocks Up Late is a natural prominent type who cannot get his favoured position in this field — if he dwells at the start or is shuffled back further than expected, his chances diminish sharply and he becomes a non-factor.

Ice Jet drops back to 2m chase for the first time on this going profile; watch his jumping under Harry Skelton — if he flukes the early fences and quickens off a slow pace he could be dangerous, but an error mid-race could end his chance immediately.

Gaelic Rambler's trainer is in strong recent form (4/16 T14) and Jonjo O'Neill Jr. excels at placing hold-up horses — watch for him making a forward move sooner than expected if he senses the pace is too tame to suit a late run.

Good ground is confirmed throughout the card at Uttoxeter — no runner has a going concern flagged, but monitor the sectionals from earlier races for any sign the ground is riding faster than Good, which would sharpen the tempo demands on Duke Of Luckley.
